tool_args.rationale: Five observations at a single setting establish a nonlinear response to u_now but cannot identify the two-hop bridge/branch dependence. Since the forecast horizon is only 0.6 relative to tau≈1, the dominant uncertainty is branch structure rather than long-horizon extrapolation; the targeted open-branch probe is the lowest-cost discriminating measurement.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit Beverton–Holt saturation using the five current rows
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The rows vary only u_now; effects of u_past, x_now, memory, gradient, and horizon remain unidentifiable, and the bridge signature suggests the open-branch response may matter.
The strongly sublinear/saturating response across u_now is inconsistent with a simple bilinear law at fixed x_now.
Higher resolution on the same setting is less useful than separating competing branch mechanisms.
Irrelevant to the target law and explicitly not worth its cost.
